correctness.rationale: A separate derivation slices the cone at y. At y=0 it gives the x-axis, and for each y≠0 it gives x=z²/y. At u≠0 the latter slice has multiplier χ(u/y)𝒢ψ(y(v−w²/(4u))) by square completion. Summing over y≠0 using the quadratic character and 𝒢²=χ(−1)q gives qχ(−D); the x-axis contributes zero. For c=0, u≠0 this is also the union multiplier: the q(q−1) frequencies D=0 vanish and q(q−1)² have magnitude q. If u=0 and w≠0, all nonzero-y slices vanish and the x-axis contributes q, canceled at c=0 by subtraction of the intersection, giving q(q−1) more zeros. On the axis u=w=0, the zero frequency is 2q²−q, and the nonzero v frequencies have magnitude q(q−1) for every c. With c≠0 and u≠0 one omits precisely the c slice from the cone sum. At D=0 this leaves magnitude √q, and at D≠0 it leaves at least q−√q>√q for q≥5. In F₃ only one nonzero-y slice remains, so its magnitude is actually √3 at every u≠0 (consistent with the source's inclusive bound). For c≠0, u=0,w≠0 the multiplier is q. The origin attains the triangle-inequality upper bound. Unitary character diagonalization of counting convolution yields the listed singular values, inverse norm and condition number; the argument works in extension fields as well.
residual_risks: The proof is for the unweighted set union and counting convolution; replacing the union by a sum or using a probability kernel changes the calculation. The F₃ interference set in the source is an enclosing set, not a claim all three values occur under the constrained frequencies.
